topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecture series, outlines the learning objectives, and frames the clinical and biological scope of cancer biology.

topics.label: Biological Foundations of Cancer and Experimental Models
topics.groupedBecause: They frame cancer as a progressive failure of normal cellular differentiation and tissue architecture driven by accumulated genetic alterations, alongside the laboratory models used to study it.

topics.label: Tumor Invasion, Metastasis, and Stepwise Malignant Progression
topics.groupedBecause: They explain the transition from localized lesions to invasive and metastatic malignancies, using colorectal tumor histology as a model of stepwise progression.

topics.label: Benign Versus Malignant Tumor Behavior and Nomenclature
topics.groupedBecause: They contrast the clinical risks of benign versus malignant neoplasms and outline the standard pathological naming conventions across tissue types.

topics.label: Pathophysiological Causes of Cancer Morbidity and Mortality
topics.groupedBecause: It explains the direct physical and systemic mechanisms through which primary and metastatic tumors impair organ function and cause fatal disease.

topics.label: Cancer Incidence and Prevalence Across Species
topics.groupedBecause: They examine the frequency and mortality patterns of different tumor types across human populations and diverse animal taxa.

topics.label: Principles and Clinical Applications of Cancer Screening
topics.groupedBecause: They assess the clinical necessity, diagnostic techniques, and variable effectiveness of population screening programs for identifying early and pre-malignant lesions.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion and Housekeeping
topics.groupedBecause: It concludes the lecture by referencing the learning outcomes and providing information on upcoming practicals and sessions.
